record.file_problem: None noted; the full technical report is present.
record.tranche_reason: The report conducts scaling-law studies using held-out validation loss against FLOPs, a similar loss-versus-compute measurement on new model families and settings.
record.gate_note: The report also describes RL-FLOPs capability curves, included as an aggregate downstream-scaling result. Other benchmark scores are not scaling-law findings and are not rows. The scaling curves are plotted, but exact loss values, exponents, fit ranges, and detailed sweep results are not stated.
record.test_reason: The report runs scaling-law sweeps as a tool to retune batch size, learning rate, tokens-per-parameter and model shape for its new architecture. Its reported result is its own model family's ~2.5× scaling-efficiency gain over Kimi K2. Figure 7 shows fitted loss-vs-FLOPs curves without exponents, values, fit ranges or any test of the power-law form. No extrapolation, compute-optimal allocation trend, shape comparison or pretraining-loss-to-downstream relation is reported. The RL-FLOPs capability curves concern post-training compute, not the pretraining scaling the versions name.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely right. The authors say their architectural, data and training changes altered the optimal regime, so they ran scaling-law studies to retune batch size, learning rate, tokens-per-parameter and model shape. The fitted curves show ~2.5× overall scaling efficiency over Kimi K2, and they adopt cosine decay over WSD under independently tuned settings.
record.recipe_differences: The study measures held-out OOD validation loss against FLOPs, but uses Kimi K2/K3 model families and their own multimodal MoE architecture, data, and training recipes. It does not provide enough detail to establish that the original fitting procedure was reproduced exactly.
record.method_sensitivity: Learning-rate schedule changes the optimal peak learning rate and batch size; the report says those optima differ substantially between cosine decay and WSD, and cosine has lower final loss under independent tuning.

fits_no_version.finding: Cosine decay and WSD have substantially different optimal peak LR and batch size at the same model size and token budget. Under independent tuning, cosine consistently reaches lower final loss.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimal hyperparameters and the ranking of LR schedules depend on tuning each schedule separately; shared hyperparameters bias schedule comparisons.

fits_no_version.finding: Scaling RL FLOPs is described as consistently improving capability scores and average tool-call steps across several evaluation areas (figure only).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Post-training RL compute yields steady capability gains across domains.

record.problems: The scaling-law curves are shown without numerical loss values, exponents, fit ranges, or uncertainty estimates. The compute-optimal allocation results are not reported, and the RL-FLOPs capability trend is only described in aggregate.

untested.parts: Power-law form of loss vs compute is shown only as a fitted curve with no exponents, ranges or fit quality; not tested.
TPP was retuned, but no compute-optimal N/D allocation or growth exponents are reported.
Model shape was retuned, but no fixed-parameter shape comparison is reported.
Native multimodal training is used, but no scaling law is reported for other modalities or regimes.
No downstream-vs-pretraining-scale or downstream-vs-pretraining-loss relation is reported.
No comparison of fitted exponents or compute-optimal splits across setups; no bending curves reported.

record.verdict_notes: This is an industrial technical report. Scaling laws serve here as an engineering tool for hyperparameter retuning and for comparing the new model with its predecessor. No numbers relevant to any version are stated in the text, and the record's V1/V6/V7 links overreach. No verdict labels are given.

versions.untested_parts: The report does not state fitted exponents or the tested parameter-count and token-count ranges; it shows fitted held-out-loss curves against FLOPs.
No explicit small-run-to-large-run prediction test is reported.
The study says it retunes tokens-per-parameter ratio and model shape, but reports no compute-optimal parameter/token allocation trend or growth exponents.
No controlled comparison of depth, width, or other architecture details at fixed parameter count is reported.
Native multimodal training is described, but no scaling-law test across modalities or other training regimes is reported.
The reported downstream-capability trend concerns RL FLOPs, not pretraining loss or pretraining scale; task-level values are not stated in the text.
Schedule-dependent optimal hyperparameters are reported, but not disagreements between fitted exponents or compute-optimal allocations, nor curves bending away from a power law.

rows.subject: Kimi K2
rows.size_stated: not stated for the scaling-law sweep; Table 1 lists 1.04T total parameters for Kimi K2
rows.operation_detail: Fitted held-out OOD validation-loss curve against FLOPs
rows.measure: Held-out OOD validation loss as a function of FLOPs
rows.note: The report presents a fitted curve, but gives no exact values, exponent, fit range, or textual description sufficient to establish its power-law shape.
rows.check: Figure-only fitted curve. No exponent, loss values, fit range or goodness of fit is given, so the power-law shape cannot be checked from the text. It is a tool-use curve, not a test.

rows.subject: Kimi K3
rows.size_stated: not stated for the scaling-law sweep; Table 1 lists 2.78T total parameters for Kimi K3
rows.operation_detail: Fitted held-out OOD validation-loss curve against FLOPs and compared scaling efficiency with Kimi K2
rows.measure: Held-out OOD validation loss versus FLOPs; overall scaling efficiency
rows.value: approximately 2.5× gain in overall scaling efficiency over Kimi K2; curve values are figure only
rows.note: The text states the efficiency gain, but does not give numerical losses, fitted exponents, or enough detail to determine whether the loss curve follows a power law.
rows.check: The 2.5× scaling-efficiency gain compares the study's own architecture and recipe with its predecessor Kimi K2. It does not bear on whether loss follows a power law, so it should not be a V1 row.

rows.subject: Kimi K3 scaling-law study
rows.operation_detail: Compared cosine decay and Warmup Stable Decay after independent scaling-law searches for each schedule
rows.measure: Final held-out loss and optimal hyperparameters
rows.baseline: WSD under its respective optimal hyperparameter settings
rows.value: Cosine decay consistently achieves lower final loss; optimal peak learning rates and batch sizes differ substantially between schedules
rows.note: This is evidence that the schedule and its tuning affect the reported loss and optimal settings; no numerical losses or hyperparameter values are provided.
rows.check: This finding is about optimal peak LR and batch size differing between cosine and WSD schedules, and cosine reaching lower final loss. It does not report schedule-dependent exponents or compute-optimal splits, so it does not measure V7. It belongs in fits_no_version.

rows.subject: Kimi K3
rows.operation_detail: Reported capability evaluations across increasing RL FLOPs

conditions.value: various public and in-house evaluations spanning knowledge, reasoning, vision, general-agent, and coding capabilities

rows.value: The report states that scaling RL FLOPs consistently improves capabilities across the listed areas; individual curve values are figure only
rows.note: Aggregate result as described in the text; the plotted evaluations are not numerically detailed there. This concerns RL scaling, not pretraining-loss predictability.
rows.check: Capability rises with RL FLOPs. That is post-training compute, not pretraining scale or pretraining loss as V6 names. Values are figure-only and the trend is described only qualitatively.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

relation.reason: The report uses scaling laws to retune training and reports approximately 2.5× efficiency over Kimi K2, without an independently assessable test of the catalog's scaling-law claims.

tranche.reason: Scaling-law searches guide the model family's hyperparameters and architecture; the reported results concern its efficiency and schedule choice, without establishing a claim version's power-law form, extrapolation, or fitted allocation.

source_check.notes: Figure 7 supplies no numerical validation losses, fitted exponents, or fit quality. The schedule comparison and RL trends are explicitly stated qualitative findings; they do not establish schedule-dependent scaling exponents or quantitative downstream predictability.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Reported capability evaluations as RL FLOPs increase
reader_labels.reason: The authors state that capability improves consistently with RL FLOPs across several areas (R4); this does not establish predictability from pretraining loss or pretraining scale.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Cosine decay versus WSD under independently tuned schedules
reader_labels.reason: The report states that optimal peak learning rates and batch sizes differ substantially by schedule and that cosine reaches lower final loss (R3).
